summary: Millrose's 2026 story is diversification bought with leverage. At 2026-09-30 it had $9.25B invested ($5.87B Lennar at a flat 8.5%; $3.37B others at 10.8%; 9.3% blended) across 156,729 homesites, 834 communities, 30 states and 22 counterparties, and it reports zero option terminations, forfeitures or renegotiation requests since inception despite the soft market. Non-Lennar pricing drifted from 11.0% (end-2025) to 10.6% (mid-2026), which management blamed on lower SOFR and a deliberate shift to stronger builders, with floors averaging about 10%; it expects about 11% in Q4 as the Dream Finders deal comes on. The defining 2026 deal is the $1.07B financing of Dream Finders' takeover of Beazer (closed 2026-10-20): $580M of land banking on about 7,000 lots plus a $488M 12% perpetual preferred, which shows Millrose will now write builder corporate paper to win the land. It also moved beyond land banking: a multifamily facility with JPI, and a $333M purchase of 1,233 finished rental homes from Lennar with 620 more under contract. Leverage rose from 26% to 36% debt-to-cap (about 40% pro forma per an analyst) against a 33% target, funded by a new unsecured $1.9B bank facility and $1.0B of 6.5%/6.75% notes; with the stock below book it will not issue equity under its own policy and has instead authorized a $250M buyback. Only a handful of counterparties are ever named (Dream Finders, JPI, Taylor Morrison's Yardly, New Home Co, Rausch Coleman); the other roughly 16 and all per-builder sizes and rates are undisclosed.

Credit facility margins after the 2026-08-05 amendment are SOFR + 1.75% / 2.00% / 2.25% by leverage. In compliance with all covenants.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q3 2026 (filed 2026-11-04), Note 11 Debt

facts.fact: SFR Secured Credit Facility dated 2026-09-30 with Goldman Sachs Bank USA (agent and initial lender): limited-recourse revolver, $235.0M committed, expandable to $1.0B, one-month Term SOFR + 1.20% with a 0.50% floor, matures 2028-09-29 with a one-year extension; $213.1M drawn.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q3 2026 (filed 2026-11-04), Note 11 Debt

facts.fact: Purchase-money mortgage structure: in 2025 Millrose bought two land parcels for $33M with non-recourse property-level mortgages that a counterparty fully indemnifies and services (pays all interest); Millrose intends to sign an option agreement with that counterparty at maturity ($4M due Q4 2026, $29M in 2027).
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q3 2026 (filed 2026-11-04), Note 11 Debt

facts.fact: 2026-07-30: Millrose closed the first acquisition under a new land-banking facility 'established by JPI and Kennedy Lewis Investment Management' to fund Class A multifamily land acquisition and development in JPI's target markets. Millrose acquires and funds development of the sites; JPI pays option fees and takes sites down as its pipeline matures. JPI (Sumitomo Forestry subsidiary) reports 54 active communities, 18,785 homes, $6.9B value. Facility size not disclosed.
facts.source_title: Millrose / JPI press release, 2026-07-30 (company IR PDF)

facts.fact: Credit ratings shown in Millrose's March 2026 deck: corporate Moody's Ba2 / S&P BB / Fitch BBB-; unsecured notes Moody's Ba3 / S&P BB / Fitch BBB-; all stable, last commented August 2025. Management said on the Q2 and Q3 2026 calls that an upgrade (investment grade) is a goal.
facts.source_title: Millrose investor presentation, March 2026 (8-K Ex. 99.1 filed 2026-02-27)

facts.fact: March 2026 deck: illustrative AFFO path from about $3.00 to about $3.30 per share on $2B of net new capital at 11% yields; total addressable market put at $170B+; margin-of-safety illustration assumes a 20% builder gross margin so a roughly 30% home-price fall before a takedown is uneconomic; positions itself against 'traditional landbank platforms' on certainty, scale and cost of capital. Builder deposits were $927.0M at 2025-12-31 (balance sheet).
facts.source_title: Millrose investor presentation, March 2026 (8-K Ex. 99.1 filed 2026-02-27)

facts.fact: Q4 2025 call (2026-02-26): Lennar's Master Program rate is fixed, subject to resets on forward deals; most other agreements float with a floor that sits roughly 50 to 200bps below the current rate; other agreements were yielding about 11% against a 6.3% cost of debt. Management's 2026 base case was about $2B of new non-Lennar capital, to about $10.5B total and over 40% outside Lennar.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q4 2025 earnings call transcript, 2026-02-26 (stockanalysis.com)

facts.fact: Q4 2025 call (2026-02-26): 96% of the portfolio by investment balance is in cross-termination pools; COO Robert Nitkin said pooling does not stop a builder walking but raises the cost. Q1 2026 call put the pooled share at about 95% of $8.7B invested capital. Management also cited about $9B of forward-flow relationships across roughly 10 counterparties.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q4 2025 earnings call transcript, 2026-02-26 (stockanalysis.com)

facts.fact: Q1 2026 call (2026-05-06): Nitkin said the average floor on option rates is about 10%; the roughly 30bp quarter-on-quarter fall in non-Lennar yield (11.0% to 10.7%) was lower SOFR, with option spreads unchanged; CEO Darren Richman said new relationships had not changed deployment rates or spreads. Average cost of debt about 6%.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q1 2026 earnings call transcript, 2026-05-06 (stockanalysis.com)

facts.fact: Q1 2026 call (2026-05-06) on competition: Richman said 'private land banking alternatives' cannot structurally match Millrose's capital certainty, and Nitkin said newer entrants to land banking would be more challenged in a tougher market. No competitor was named on any 2026 call.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q1 2026 earnings call transcript, 2026-05-06 (stockanalysis.com)

facts.fact: Q2 2026 call (2026-08-04): Nitkin attributed the dip in non-Lennar yield to 10.6% to a deliberate mix shift toward stronger builders and less development complexity, and called 10bp moves normal. Richman said banks are pulling back from the sector and builder demand exceeds capital supply, letting Millrose be patient. Organic deployment was described as about $400M a quarter, about $500M including M&A.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q2 2026 earnings call transcript, 2026-08-04 (stockanalysis.com)

facts.fact: Q2 2026 call (2026-08-04): Richman said deposits are about 10% today versus roughly 20 to 25% historically, framing the lower level as offset by other credit enhancement (pooling); Millrose underwrites to a 20%+ builder gross margin assuming flat home prices. He noted several public builders had booked walk-away charges on parcels elsewhere, and that Millrose's fallback plans if a builder walked are re-optioning to another (possibly larger) builder or selling to a merchant builder. (Machine transcript; wording approximate.)
facts.source_title: Millrose Q2 2026 earnings call transcript, 2026-08-04 (stockanalysis.com)

facts.fact: Q3 2026 call (2026-10-27): management said no customer has terminated, threatened to terminate or asked to renegotiate, including on the roughly $800M of land that cycled in Q3. Nitkin said builders, including top-15 builders Millrose does not yet work with, are approaching it to take over land positions that are being renegotiated with other capital providers; Millrose had not yet done such a deal.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings call transcript, 2026-10-27 (stockanalysis.com)

facts.fact: Q3 2026 call (2026-10-27): Nitkin expects the non-Lennar yield to reach about 11% in Q4 2026 (from 10.8%) on higher SOFR and new deals including Dream Finders; agreements are generally floating with floors. He said the Beazer land was bought at a discount to Beazer's prior book value (amount not given).
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings call transcript, 2026-10-27 (stockanalysis.com)

facts.fact: Q3 2026 call (2026-10-27): an analyst (Goldman Sachs) estimated about 40% debt-to-capitalization pro forma for Dream Finders, which management did not dispute; Richman said takedown proceeds will repay debt back toward the unchanged 33% target (no timeline) and that M&A portfolios turn faster (about 2 years versus 3). Buybacks will not be debt-funded: while the stock trades below book, about 90% of earnings is distributed and about 10% goes to repurchases, with the dividend not reduced, plus unused Lennar 'priority capital'.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings call transcript, 2026-10-27 (stockanalysis.com)

facts.fact: Q3 2026 call (2026-10-27): the SFR pilot was underwritten at about a 5% going-in cap rate and 10 to 12% levered IRR, is about 1% of assets, and is described as a first step toward a possible rent-to-own product; Richman said Lennar did not push Millrose into it and the deal was arm's length. He said no Kennedy Lewis vehicle outside Millrose took part in the Dream Finders financing. Lennar's book was described as about $6B of assets with roughly $4B of build-out cost still to fund.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings call transcript, 2026-10-27 (Webull / Motley Fool)

facts.fact: Q2 2026 call (2026-08-04): Richman said a new residential product suite was in development (commercial ruled out) and that the 33% leverage target, set before Millrose had operating history, was under review; the Taylor Morrison / Yardly arrangement included vertical construction financing, unlike JPI.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q2 2026 earnings call transcript, 2026-08-04 (stockanalysis.com)

facts.fact: Q1 2026 call (2026-05-06): the $284M development loan repaid in early April 2026 was cross-collateralized by multiple Florida communities; the new Q1 counterparty was described as a top-10 publicly traded national homebuilder (not named). Market colour: Texas challenged by high inventory; builders cutting spec inventory.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q1 2026 earnings call transcript, 2026-05-06 (stockanalysis.com)

builder_relationships.description: Master Program Agreement: $5,874.2M invested capital at 2026-09-30 (63.5% of total; down from $6,102.0M at 2025-12-31) at a flat 8.5% weighted-average yield, 3.8-year remaining life. 2026 year-to-date fundings $1,636.4M and takedown proceeds $1,864.3M (sum of Q1-Q3). Also sold Millrose 1,233 completed homes (about $333M) for the single-family rental pilot, and agreed 2026-08-27 Founder's Rights Agreement amendments carving BTR out of its capital priority/consent rights.
builder_relationships.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings press release (8-K Ex. 99.1, 2026-10-27)

builder_relationships.description: Financing of Dream Finders' acquisition of Beazer Homes (announced 2026-05-11, closed 2026-10-20), $1,068M in total: $580M (net of Dream Finders option deposits) of land banking on about 7,000 former Beazer homesites, more than half finished, about 2.5-year weighted-average life, earning option fees plus an $8.0M commitment fee; plus a $488M (net of OID; $500M balance) Dream Finders preferred instrument at a 12% dividend with a $5.25M commitment fee, funded $171M on 2026-09-14 and $317M at closing.
builder_relationships.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 Earnings Presentation (8-K Ex. 99.2, 2026-10-27), slide 12

Pricing by counterparty or by credit quality: not disclosed; only the Lennar / Other / total weighted-average yields are published. Actual option-rate spreads and individual floors are not public (floor commentary comes from call transcripts only).
JPI facility size, number of sites and yield: not disclosed in the 2026-07-30 release or the Q2 materials.

Dream Finders land-banking option rate and deposit percentage: not disclosed (only $580M net of deposits, an $8.0M commitment fee, about 7,000 lots). The full preferred terms would be in Dream Finders' own filings, which were not opened.
